intro: Bundesliga basement boys Borussia Mönchengladbach will look to improve on their record-breaking poor start when they welcome an unbeaten Borussia Dortmund.
h2h: Dortmund might be unbeaten in six of the last seven competitive H2Hs at any venue, but since the start of the 2020/21 season, they have lost four of their six Bundesliga away games (W1, D1, L4) against Gladbach. Against no other side have they suffered more away league reversals in that time.
datos: Gladbach scored first in only two league games this season and went on to lose both.
Eight of Gladbach’s nine league games this season produced over 2.5 goals.
Dortmund have conceded six of their last seven domestic goals after the hour mark.
Dortmund have scored 13 of their 16 league goals this season in the second half.
Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Shūto Machino’s five league goals for Gladbach all arrived beyond half-time and he has scored against Dortmund before (for Holstein Kiel), but with his joint-club-high three yellow cards contributing to Gladbach’s joint-league-high 24 bookings, maybe another booking is more likely than a goal. Felix Nmecha has already equalled his best Bundesliga return of four goals from 2024/25 with a brace on the previous matchday, with both goals coming from outside of the box to make him only the third Dortmund player to do so in one league match.
Kō Itakura serves a suspension for Gladbach, while Dortmund’s Carney Chukwuemeka and Serhou Guirassy are injury doubts.
For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.
Logic dictates that Dortmund are worthy favourites, but the reset of the international window hints at the draw being a potential route to value given Gladbach’s strong home H2H form.
